# Sansera Engineering - Institutional Stock Research Report - 30 July 2026

Company: Sansera Engineering Limited

Ticker: SANSERA

Report date: 30 July 2026

Research posture: High-quality diversification story at a demanding valuation

Investment stance: Credible aerospace-led re-rating, but the price already assumes flawless execution

Conviction score: 58 / 100

Multibagger potential: 52 / 100

Potential trap risk: 46 / 100

## 1. Executive Verdict

Sansera Engineering is a precision-engineering company in the middle of a deliberate and so far successful transformation. Its foundation is one of the world's top-ten connecting-rod and forged-component franchises supplying global automotive OEMs. Its future, and the reason the stock has roughly doubled in 2026, is the Aerospace, Defence and Semiconductor (ADS) business, which grew about 155% in FY26 and carries an unexecuted order backlog of roughly INR 4,464 crore - more than fourteen times the segment's FY26 revenue.

FY26 was a genuine operational inflection. Consolidated revenue rose about 16% to INR 3,498 crore, EBITDA margin expanded a full percentage point to 18.1%, and profit after tax jumped 51% to about INR 327 crore. The fourth quarter was stronger still, with revenue up 28% and PAT up 108% year-on-year. Operating cash flow of about INR 387 crore broadly tracked reported profit, which is an important quality signal for a capex-heavy manufacturer.

The tension in the investment case is entirely about price and return on capital. At around INR 3,185 (24 July 2026), the stock trades near 60x trailing consolidated earnings while reported ROE is still only around 10-11%. Investors are paying an aerospace-platform multiple today for a company whose profit pool is still roughly two-thirds automotive ICE. The gap must be closed by execution: the ADS ramp toward management's INR 550-600 crore FY27 target, continued margin expansion toward 20%, and rising capital efficiency.

Final view: Sansera is a serious, well-run diversification story with real multi-year order visibility, not a narrative stock. But after a roughly 100% year-to-date move, the share price has raced ahead of current profitability. It belongs on an active watchlist or as a staggered accumulation with strict valuation discipline, with the just-published June-2026 quarter results as the immediate checkpoint.

## 2. Business Overview

Sansera manufactures complex, high-precision forged and machined components. The legacy business supplies connecting rods, rocker arms, crankshafts and similar engine and chassis parts to automotive OEMs across India, Europe and North America, where it ranks among the top ten global suppliers of connecting rods. These are qualification-heavy, tolerance-critical parts where vendor approval takes years, giving the franchise more stickiness than generic auto ancillaries.

The company reports three end-use segments. In the fourth quarter of FY26, Auto-ICE contributed about 68.5% of revenue, Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV about 13%, and Non-Auto about 18.5%. Management's stated direction is to take the non-auto share materially higher - the strategic ambition discussed publicly is a roughly 40% non-auto mix over time, with Auto-ICE drifting toward 60% or below.

The growth engine inside Non-Auto is ADS - aerospace, defence and semiconductor components. Sansera is a Tier-1 supplier to Boeing and a Tier-2 supplier to Airbus, and the segment generated about INR 315 crore in FY26, up around 155% year-on-year, with a Q4 run-rate near INR 110 crore. The unexecuted ADS order backlog of about INR 4,464 crore provides multi-year revenue visibility that very few Indian auto-ancillary peers possess. Geographically the business is diversifying as well: international revenue grew about 47% in Q4 FY26, with Europe around 21% and the US around 10% of sales.

## 3. Investment Thesis

The investment case rests on five pillars.

### 3.1 Qualification-Heavy Precision Niche

Connecting rods, aero-structures and defence components are not commodity castings. Customer qualification cycles, metallurgy, machining accuracy and delivery reliability create real switching costs. Sansera's three-decade automotive track record is the credibility base from which the aerospace franchise is being built.

### 3.2 ADS Backlog-Led Growth

The roughly INR 4,464 crore unexecuted ADS backlog against INR 315 crore of FY26 segment revenue is the single most important number in the thesis. Management guides ADS revenue to INR 550-600 crore in FY27 - nearly doubling again. If this converts on schedule, the highest-margin, highest-multiple part of the business compounds far faster than the group.

### 3.3 Margin Expansion Underway

EBITDA margin moved from about 17.1% in FY25 to 18.1% in FY26, and reached 19.3% in Q4 FY26. Richer ADS mix, operating leverage and gross-margin gains (about 41.9% in Q4) support management's "20-20-20" aspiration - 20% EBITDA margin, 20% growth, 20% ROCE. The margin trajectory is the clearest evidence the mix shift is real.

### 3.4 Clean Balance Sheet and Cash Conversion

Reported debt-to-equity is negligible (around 0.03x on the latest data snapshot) after the late-2024 institutional fundraise, and FY26 operating cash flow of about INR 387 crore exceeded reported PAT of about INR 327 crore. The company can fund its aerospace capacity build-out without balance-sheet stress.

### 3.5 Long-Cycle Strategic Sector Exposure

Aerospace and defence are supply-constrained, multi-year-visibility industries where India is gaining share as a manufacturing base. Sansera's early qualification with Boeing and Airbus positions it for a demand wave that is largely independent of the auto cycle.

## 4. Financial Performance

| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | FY26 | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | INR 998.7 crore | INR 781.7 crore | INR 3,497.9 crore | Q4 growth of 28% YoY; full-year growth about 16%. Momentum accelerated through the year. |
| EBITDA | INR 192.9 crore | INR 127.1 crore | INR 632.1 crore | Q4 EBITDA up 52% YoY; full-year margin 18.1% vs 17.1% in FY25. |
| EBITDA margin | 19.3% | 16.3% | 18.1% | About 300 bps of Q4 expansion; mix shift and operating leverage are visible. |
| PAT | INR 123.1 crore | INR 59.2 crore | INR 326.9 crore | Q4 PAT up 108% YoY; full-year PAT up 51% from INR 216.9 crore. |
| Operating cash flow | - | - | INR 387.1 crore | OCF above PAT; healthy accrual quality for a capex-heavy year. |
| ADS segment revenue | INR 109.7 crore | - | INR 315.5 crore | Up about 155% YoY; the growth engine of the thesis. |

Two caveats keep this from being an unqualified endorsement. First, the year's strength is back-loaded: Q4 accounted for a disproportionate share of the FY26 profit jump, and one strong quarter does not establish a permanent base. Second, the Q1 FY27 result (quarter ended June 2026) was published around 25 July 2026 and must be reviewed immediately - the thesis assumes the FY26 exit momentum carried into the new year, and that assumption is currently unverified.

## 5. Financial Quality

Signs of financial strength:

- Revenue growth accelerated through FY26 and reached 28% YoY in Q4.
- PAT grew three times faster than revenue in FY26, evidencing operating leverage.
- Operating cash flow exceeded reported PAT in FY26.
- Leverage is negligible; the aerospace build-out is being funded from equity and internal accruals.
- Gross margin around 42% reflects genuine engineering value-add, not commodity conversion.

Areas requiring monitoring:

- Reported ROE of about 10-11% and ROCE of about 14% are modest for a 60x multiple; the equity base was enlarged by the late-2024 fundraise and must now be sweated.
- Aerospace working capital and qualification costs can rise ahead of revenue.
- The FY26 profit surge leaned on an exceptional Q4; sustainability needs two to four more quarters of proof.
- Segment-level margin disclosure for ADS is limited; the mix-improvement story is partly inferred.

Financial quality score: 6.5 / 10

## 6. Industry Opportunity

Sansera sits at the intersection of three demand pools. Global automotive ICE components is a mature, cyclical, slowly eroding pool where Sansera wins by consolidation of share among qualified suppliers. Tech-agnostic and xEV components let content-per-vehicle survive powertrain transition. Aerospace, defence and semiconductor equipment components are the structural opportunity: global aerospace supply chains are capacity-constrained, deliveries are sold out years ahead, and India is emerging as a credible precision-manufacturing base with policy tailwinds in defence indigenisation.

The exciting part of the runway is that Sansera's ADS backlog already exists - this is not a hoped-for market but contracted work awaiting execution. The risk is the mirror image: the market may be capitalising the aerospace story faster than the P&L can deliver it, and ICE - still about two-thirds of revenue - remains exposed to global auto cycles, tariff disruptions and the long-run EV transition.

Industry runway score: 7.5 / 10

## 7. Management And Execution

Management, led by co-founder promoters and a professional leadership team, has articulated a clear and measurable strategy: diversify from ICE toward a 40% non-auto mix, scale ADS revenue to INR 550-600 crore in FY27, and pursue the "20-20-20" framework, with a stated long-term ambition of roughly INR 8,000-10,000 crore of revenue by the end of the decade. The CEO described FY26 as an inflection point, and the reported numbers back that language.

Execution will be judged on five outcomes:

1. Whether ADS revenue actually reaches INR 550-600 crore in FY27 and the backlog converts on schedule.
2. Whether EBITDA margin holds above 18-19% while capacity scales.
3. Whether ROCE climbs toward the high teens as the enlarged equity base is deployed.
4. Whether working capital stays disciplined through the aerospace ramp.
5. Whether customer concentration inside ADS broadens beyond the anchor aerospace programmes.

The governance record is clean on the evidence available, but promoter shareholding has declined from about 34.8% in mid-2024 to 29.21% as of June 2026 - a combination of dilution from the late-2024 institutional placement and a roughly 2-million-share promoter-group sale in October 2025. This is not disqualifying, but a promoter group reducing at all-time highs while the market pays a premium multiple deserves ongoing attention, alongside pledges, related-party items and auditor notes at each annual review.

Management and governance score: 6.5 / 10

## 8. Ownership Quality

The ownership structure as of the June 2026 exchange filing: promoters 29.21% (down from 30.10% in March 2026 and about 34.8% two years earlier), FIIs about 21.5% and rising, mutual funds about 22.9% but reduced from 26.3% in early 2025, other domestic institutions taking total institutional holding above 50%, and public/other holders around 18%.

The positive interpretation is deep institutional sponsorship: more than half the company is held by institutions, foreign ownership has been rising through 2026, and the late-2024 placement brought in long-only global funds at around INR 1,200 per share. The cautionary reading is that the two most informed holder classes - promoters and domestic mutual funds - have both been net reducers into the 2026 rally, while momentum-following flows carried the price. Neither signal is decisive alone; together they argue for buying discipline rather than chase.

Ownership score: 6.0 / 10

## 9. Valuation

Valuation is the central risk in Sansera.

At about INR 3,185 (24 July 2026) with a market capitalisation around INR 20,200 crore, the stock trades at roughly 60x FY26 consolidated earnings (about INR 52 per share on an enlarged base of roughly 6.3 crore shares) and about 6.3x book value - against reported ROE of only 10-11%. The multiple already embeds several years of the ADS story. The stock has roughly doubled year-to-date in 2026 and is up well over 200% in three years, so entry price - not business quality - is where money is most likely to be lost from here.

The business can grow into this valuation only if earnings compound rapidly while the aerospace mix keeps the multiple elevated. If growth normalises before earnings catch up, the derating math is severe: at a market-average industrial multiple the stock would halve even with no profit decline.

### Valuation Scenarios

| Scenario | Business outcome | FY30 EPS potential | Reasonable multiple | Implied price range | Probability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bear case | ICE cyclically weak; ADS ramp slips to FY28+; margin back to about 17%; EPS compounds below 10% | INR 65-75 | 28-32x | INR 1,850-2,350 | 25% |
| Base case | Revenue compounds mid-teens; ADS hits FY27 guidance and keeps scaling; EBITDA margin 19-20%; EPS compounds about 20% | INR 100-110 | 35-42x | INR 3,500-4,600 | 50% |
| Bull case | 20-20-20 broadly delivered; backlog converts early; non-auto approaches 40% mix; aerospace platform rating persists | INR 130-145 | 45-55x | INR 5,900-7,900 | 25% |

The probability-weighted picture implies mid-single-digit to low-double-digit annualised returns from the current price - positive but unexceptional for the execution risk being underwritten. The risk-reward improves materially on any meaningful correction toward the mid-INR 2,000s, where the base case would offer a genuine margin of safety.

Valuation score: 3.5 / 10

## 10. Multibagger Potential

Sansera has most of the structural ingredients of a long-horizon multibagger: a defensible precision niche, a contracted growth backlog, margin expansion, negligible debt, credible management ambition and exposure to a supply-constrained global aerospace cycle from a low base.

What the current price takes away is the easy path. A stock at 60x trailing earnings can no longer multiply through rerating; from here, returns must come almost entirely from earnings compounding.

### What Must Happen For 5x Potential

- Revenue must travel from about INR 3,500 crore toward the INR 8,000-10,000 crore decade-end ambition, implying mid-to-high-teens compounding for the group.
- ADS must scale from INR 315 crore to well beyond INR 1,500 crore, with the backlog refilling as it executes.
- EBITDA margin must hold at or above 20% as aerospace mix rises.
- ROE/ROCE must climb from about 11%/14% into the high teens, proving the enlarged capital base earns its keep.
- Cash conversion must remain near or above 100% of PAT through the capex cycle.
- Promoter selling must stop, and dilution must remain minimal.

### What Must Happen For 10x Potential

A 10x outcome from the 30 July 2026 reference price and valuation base requires Sansera to become a globally significant aerospace and defence components platform - a multi-programme Tier-1 supplier across Boeing, Airbus and defence primes with semiconductor-equipment optionality - rather than an Indian auto-ancillary with an aerospace arm. That means multiple backlog refresh cycles, sustained 20%+ compounding for close to a decade, and durable premium margins. The evidence today supports a plausible 3-5x over a long horizon on excellent execution; it does not yet support underwriting 10x from the 30 July 2026 entry price.

Multibagger probability: Moderate.
5x potential: Possible over a long horizon, execution- and entry-price-dependent.
10x potential: Not yet underwritten.

## 11. Potential Trap Analysis

Sansera does not resemble a debt trap, an accounting trap or a governance trap on current evidence: leverage is negligible, FY26 cash flow exceeded profit, and disclosures are institutional-grade.

The live risk is a valuation trap with a momentum overlay. The stock's 2026 doubling has been driven substantially by the aerospace narrative and strong Q4 optics. If ADS conversion slips even one year, or EBITDA margin stalls below 19%, the earnings path cannot support 60x, and the two most informed holder groups (promoters, domestic MFs) have already been reducing into strength.

### Trap Warning Signs

- Q1 FY27 or subsequent quarters show revenue growth decelerating below the mid-teens.
- ADS revenue tracking materially below the INR 550-600 crore FY27 guidance.
- EBITDA margin falling back below 17-18%.
- Working capital or receivables rising faster than sales during the aerospace ramp.
- Operating cash flow diverging below reported PAT.
- Further promoter-group selling, or any pledge creation.
- Backlog stagnating - execution without replenishment ends the visibility argument.
- ROCE failing to improve despite the capex coming onstream.

Trap verdict: Not an operational trap today; clear valuation-trap risk if execution merely meets, rather than beats, expectations.

## 13. Key Risks

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Monitoring trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Valuation derating | High | High | Growth or margin misses while the stock trades near 60x earnings. |
| ADS execution slippage | Medium | High | Segment revenue tracking below guidance; backlog conversion delays. |
| Auto-ICE cyclical downturn or tariff disruption | Medium | High | About two-thirds of revenue remains ICE-linked; global OEM volumes and trade policy. |
| Promoter stake reduction continuing | Medium | Medium-High | Further SAST disclosures of promoter-group sales or pledges. |
| Working-capital stress in aerospace ramp | Medium | Medium | Receivables/inventory growth outpacing revenue. |
| Customer concentration in aerospace programmes | Medium | Medium | Dependence on a small number of anchor platforms. |
| Modest return ratios persisting | Medium | Medium | ROE stuck near 10-11% two years after the capital raise. |

## 14. Stock Monitoring Checklist

- Did the June-2026 quarter sustain revenue growth in the high teens or better?
- Is ADS revenue on the path to INR 550-600 crore for FY27?
- Did EBITDA margin hold above 18-19%?
- Is the unexecuted order backlog being replenished as it converts?
- Is operating cash flow still tracking at or above reported PAT?
- Are receivables and inventory growing slower than sales?
- Has promoter holding stabilised at 29.2%, and are there any new pledges?
- Are mutual funds still net sellers, or has domestic institutional selling abated?
- Is ROCE visibly improving as aerospace capacity utilises?
- Is the stock still priced for perfection relative to delivered earnings?

## 15. Final Recommendation

Sansera Engineering should be classified as a high-quality structural diversification story on an active watchlist, suitable for staggered accumulation only with valuation discipline. The business is executing: FY26 delivered accelerating growth, real margin expansion, cash-backed profits and a transformational aerospace backlog. This is one of the more credible ICE-to-aerospace transitions in the Indian mid-cap universe.

The stock is a different matter from the business. After roughly doubling in 2026, it trades near 60x trailing earnings against an 11% ROE, promoters and domestic funds have been trimming into the rally, and the newest quarter's numbers are not yet assessed. Fresh capital at the current price is underwriting near-flawless execution.

Recommended stance: Watchlist / accumulate only on meaningful corrections or clear evidence of guidance-beating ADS execution.
Best investor fit: Patient growth investors who will track quarterly execution closely and can tolerate a derating drawdown.
Not suitable for: Value investors requiring margin of safety, or anyone extrapolating the 2026 price momentum.
Upgrade trigger: ADS revenue at or above the FY27 guidance run-rate with backlog replenishment, EBITDA margin at or above 19-20%, ROCE inflecting upward, and promoter selling ceasing - or a valuation reset toward the mid-INR 2,000s with the thesis intact.
Downgrade trigger: ADS guidance miss, margin fade below 17-18%, cash conversion deteriorating, continued promoter reduction, or backlog stagnation.

Immediate next diligence: read the Q1 FY27 (June 2026) results and earnings-call commentary published in late July 2026; verify the FY26 consolidated figures against the annual report when released; obtain segment-level ADS margins; and build a peer comparison against Indian auto-ancillary and aerospace-supply peers on growth, ROCE and valuation before sizing any position.

This report is research support, not investment advice. All figures should be verified against primary filings before any investment decision.
